design: docs/designs/massive_rows/DESIGN.md section 4 (the pin, re-derived by the accumulator rule on the engine's own Bresenham lines, the round-2 map docs/designs/massive_rows/massive_rows_round2_map.py); DERIVATIONS_BEAM section 23.3; every number pinned before the run, none moved after it

integers.energy_note: E' = isqrt(E'_0^2 + 3 p_D . p_D) = 4113 on every direction of the pin's table (abs(p_D) 219.32 to 220.64)

byte_identity.note: the gate of the identity (tests/test_massive_rows.py (a)): the amplitude worlds mz_345, bell_0_8 and slits_low of series L's generator (examples/events/amplitude/make_worlds.py) run through the runner at their declared ticks, the sha256 of state.json, of the books (the audit of run.json, JSON-encoded) and of events.jsonl, registered from the base tree before the build (main 65b65f45, the design's head b1248102) and read after it: every world without the key reads as it did, byte for byte, the pair (f_F, q_F) = (1, 0) on every family and acc_turn omitted from the row's record; a law change re-registers them (the script scratchpad's digests.py, the same runner)

lamp_leg.line: the age of the 11th Link of the lamp's diagonals (1, +-1, 0) by the accumulator rule, (2 tau x 624 + 4113) // 8226 >= 11; the first birth at tick 1, so the first `rerelease` line at an opening at tick 140 (the photon's 14); GAMEBOARD

screen_60.line: the first `click` line of `matter` at the detector `screen_60` (a row's arrival, the group pace: 815 intervals after the re-release at 140); DETECTOR

screen_37.line: the first `click` line at `screen_37` (876 after the re-release); DETECTOR

longest_row.line: the intervals of the fan's longest row, (17, 26, 0) to the y face at (51, 121), after its re-release; a record born at the tick b completes about b + 139 + 1468; GAMEBOARD

bands.line: the bright bands' centres in pixels, the count-weighted means of the gathers' chosen `screen_<y>` over the bands 30..43, 53..67, 77..90 (7.1's exact two-path law at lambda = 4.6545); DETECTOR

pearson.line: Pearson of the gathers' counts per pixel (the chosen `screen_<y>` of the records 1..4096) with the two-source cosine 1 + cos(2 pi (l_2 - l_1) / lambda) over the 121 pixels; the map's 0.886, the registered photon's 0.891 on this fan; DETECTOR

visibility.line: (bright - dark) / (bright + dark) of the mean counts over the cosine's bright pixels 35..38, 59..61, 82..85 and its dark pixels 13..20, 48..50, 70..72, 100..107; the map's weights 0.965; DETECTOR

dark.line: every dark pixel's count 0 to 3 (the map's expected 0 to 2.3); DETECTOR

slits_matter.refutes: a band off by more than one pixel (the wavelength not h / p); the centre's first `click` line off by more than 5 intervals of 955 (the pace not p / E'); no fringes (the phase not p . x)
slits_matter.diagnostics: the records whose completion the ladder places at a face (about a third on the photon's lines and amounts) or at the wall's own sets (x = 7 and 8) are a GAMEBOARD diagnostic reported beside the pin, not a reading of it; the screen's gathers are the detector reading

slits_matter_1024.note: the run the Boss ordered first (the design's section 7): the same pin read on the 1024 gathers of the records 1..1024, the cells' widths a quarter of the pin's; the timing lines the same (the lamp leg, the first `click` lines, the longest row)

slits_matter_small.note: the register's replay (tests/test_massive_rows.py (f)): the world's gathers, the books at the end and the digests of the run, written by the engine as shipped (replay_register.py, no number typed by hand) and replayed bit-exact
